text.p: Bonds recovered from lows to move into positive territory with traders seeing some potential upside due to the widened spread with Bunds. The 10-year spread stood at 74 basis points up from 73 at Thursday's close. Friday was a holiday in much of Europe.

"From 74 basis points, our 10 year bonds become a good buy," said one trader. This limited the fall which was initially totally produced by Spain," said one trader. The spread with Spain's 10-year Bono was holding steady at six basis points.
Traders said that there were no particular domestic factors affecting the market.

The Bank of Portugal was not expected to cuts when it sets money market conditions later on Monday. "There are no domestic factors...so we have to keep a close eye on the Bund. I don't see the long end losing ground," said another trader.
Eyes were also on the U.S. Federal Reserve even if the betting was that there would be no rate rise on Tuesday.

There was greater concern about an eventual rate rise in Germany and it was this that had driven the dollar down against the mark, traders said. But even if the Bundesbank did eventually raise its repo rate, the Portuguese market would suffer greatly as room was still seen for local rate cuts.
